**The Last Letter**

I found it tucked between the pages of an old, leather-bound book—yellowed with age, the kind of book that smells like dust and forgotten stories. The letter was written in a hand I didn’t recognize, though the script was familiar. It was addressed to me, but I had no memory of ever knowing the writer.

The envelope bore no stamp, no date, just my name in elegant, looping cursive. Inside, the paper was brittle, the ink faded but still legible.

*"Dear [Your Name],*

*I don’t know if you’ll ever read this. If you do, it means I’m already gone. I hope you’re well. I hope you remember me. I was the one who gave you that first book, the one with the red cover and the story about a girl who could walk through walls. You laughed when I told you it was real. You didn’t believe me. But it was. And now, I’m sorry I never told you the truth about it.*

*I was the one who wrote it. I was the girl who walked through walls. I was the one who left you that book, hoping you’d find it someday. I was the one who wanted you to know the magic was real. But I couldn’t tell you. Not then. Not when you were too young to understand.*

*I’m sorry I didn’t stay. I’m sorry I didn’t tell you everything. But I hope, just once, you believe me. The magic was real. And I loved you. Always.*

*Yours,*
*[A Name I Don’t Remember]"*

I held the letter to my chest, my fingers trembling. The book I’d been reading—*The Girl Who Walked Through Walls*—was still open on the table. The last page was blank. Just like the last page of my life.

I closed the book gently, the spine creaking. The letter slipped from my fingers and landed on the floor. I picked it up again, running my thumb over the words one last time.

And then I burned it.

The flames licked at the edges, turning the paper black before my eyes. The scent of smoke filled the room, sharp and acrid. I watched as the last remnants of the letter turned to ash, carried away by the draft from the open window.

I didn’t believe in magic.

But sometimes, I wonder if I ever did.
